sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:56
items.html:
Ten kinds of vessels. The root of all the vessels is phase four
The first kind is phase four of the four phases of direct light, which is the root of all the vessels in the worlds, and it is the secret of the Malchut of Ein Sof [infinity], where the first restriction took place. Before the restriction she clothed all four phases of direct light, which is the secret of the upper light filling the whole of reality, and there was no aspect of reception apart from her. And after she was restricted and was corrected with a screen, so that she is found coupling with the upper light in the secret of a coupling by striking, and she raises reflected light — now this reflected light becomes an aspect of a vessel of reception in her place. As written in the words of the ARI (in Part 3, Chapter 1, Items 1, 2, 3, etc., and in Chapter 12, Item 4).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:57
items.html:
After the restriction phase four was included in the screen, and the reflected light became a vessel in her place
And you should know that the aforementioned phase four is the vessel itself even after the restriction — that is, the coarseness in her; except that this coarseness is no longer fit for reception from the restriction onward, unless she is included in the screen. And then the reflected light that she raises is measured precisely by the coarseness in her, and according to the measure of the abundance of the coarseness in her, so is the magnitude of the measure of the light that she raises; for this reflected light becomes a vessel of reception to the measure of the magnitude of the level of the upper light, as written at length (in Inner Observation, Part 2).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:58
items.html:
The expansion of the light and its departure caused the existence of vessels
Now the ARI establishes for us a great rule: “for the cause of the expansion of the light and its departure afterwards brought about the coming into being of a vessel” (here, Chapter 1, Item 9). Yet there is indeed something to understand in his words: surely the first expansion too requires a vessel, even before it departed, for there is no light without a vessel. And his words may be resolved according to what he writes below (Chapter 6, Item 2), that the first expansion which issued from the Peh [mouth] of AK outward issued entirely mixed together — meaning that the light and the vessel were mixed one with the other, and the vessel was not discernible before the departure, although it is necessarily there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:59
items.html:
The expansion and the departure are equal causes in the making of the vessel
Indeed this resolution is somewhat forced, for the wording “brought about the coming into being of a vessel” does not sit well, since the wording implies that before the departure there is as yet no existence of a vessel at all. Rather, we must go deeper into his words. And in truth his words are very carefully weighed, for he did not say that the cause of the departure of the light brought about the making of a vessel, but says that the cause of the expansion of the light and its departure brought about the making of a vessel. The implication is that both of them — the expansion and the departure — are equal causes in the making of the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:60
items.html:
The first matter of the vessel is phase four
And his words are understood together with what was explained above (in Items 56 and 57), that the first matter of the vessel is phase four, upon which the first restriction took place. The meaning of this is the greatness of the will to receive that was included in the light of Ein Sof [infinity], called by the name Malchut of Ein Sof; and in Ein Sof she was not discernible at all. The beginning of her revelation was after she had been restricted and had become a vacant space, for then the greatness of the will to receive was revealed, to the aspect of oppositeness of form towards the upper light, which is wholly to bestow and has in it not even the least trace of the will to receive. And by this she was separated, and descended, and became distanced from the upper light from one extreme to the other; for disparity of form is the spiritual distinction, and oppositeness of form is complete separation from one extreme to the other in spirituality. Therefore, from then onward, this greatness of the will to receive in the restricted phase four is regarded as the greatness of the coarseness in the worlds, over against the upper light, which is regarded as the utmost refinement in reality — and this only from the aspect of being clean of the will to receive, since it is wholly to bestow. Beyond this we have no attainment in the upper light with respect to His self. And we have already elaborated on this in Part 1 (in Inner Light and in Inner Observation), and there is no need to elaborate further here.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:61
items.html:
After the restriction phase four is included in the screen, and the reflected light rising by means of both of them becomes a vessel of reception
Now, for all the far separation of phase four from the upper light, as above, there is no vessel of reception at all apart from her; only she requires the correction of a screen. And then, just as before the restriction she received by the aspect of the magnitude of the drawing alone, so in that same measure she now receives by the aspect of the magnitude of the quantity of the rejection — that is, according to the measure of the magnitude of the light that she would have been able to receive had she not been limited by restriction and screen. (And here you must understand well the meaning of the words restriction and screen; and see the Table of Answers in Part 2, answer 43.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:62
items.html:
The departure of the light from phase four was the cause of the emergence of the screen
And it has already been explained in Part 2 that the Malchut of circles, upon which the restriction took place, is the root and the cause of the Malchut of straightness and of the screen in her. For after the light departed from the Malchut of circles, from all four phases in her, she returned to draw the light to the three phases in her upon which there had been no restriction; and this will is the secret of the correction of the screen, so that the light shall not expand to phase four in her, but precisely up to three phases and no more. And this came about for her because of the departure of the light from all four phases in her, so that she remained entirely empty of light, as written (ibid.). And you find that the departure of the light was the cause of the birth of the screen.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:63
items.html:
Phase four is a product of the expansion of the upper light. Thus the expansion and the departure together brought about the making of a vessel, for phase four and the screen issued from them
Indeed phase four in herself is a product of the expansion of the light, for she is phase four of direct light and is the secret of the Malchut of Ein Sof [infinity], as above; only that the light afterwards departed from her, in the secret of the restriction, as above. Thus phase four in her very self is a product of the expansion of the light, and the screen is a product of the departure of the light. And it was explained in Item 61 that from the restriction onward the two of them join together — namely, phase four and the screen — into an aspect of a vessel of reception, and apart from them there is no vessel of reception at all in the worlds. You see how correct are the words of the ARI cited above, who says “for the cause of the expansion of the light and its departure afterwards brought about the coming into being of a vessel”: for from the expansion of the light phase four in herself is drawn, that is, the aspect of the coarseness in her, and from the departure of the light the aspect of the screen corrected in her is drawn, without which she is not fit for reception at all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:64
items.html:
Since the beginning of the coming into being of the vessel came from expansion and departure, every vessel must therefore be preceded by these two forces
And it is known that all the forces in the upper ones must be found in those lower than them. Therefore, since the beginning of the coming into being of the vessel — that is, in the Malchut of straightness, which is the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh [head] of AK — came from the cause of the expansion of the light and its departure, as above, from there onward every vessel must be preceded by these two causes, namely the expansion of the light and its departure; and no vessel in the worlds can be pictured apart from them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:65
items.html:
The matter of the vessel is the coarseness, and the form is the screen
Now the fundamental matter and form of the vessel have been well explained, which are: the coarseness of phase four, which is the matter, and the screen that was corrected in her, which is the form. From these two, all the kinds of vessels cascaded, in their generality and in their particularity, in all four worlds: ABYA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:66
items.html:
The second kind is the reflected light rising from the Peh upward and clothing the ten Sefirot of direct light
The second kind of the vessels is the reflected light that rises from below upward by a coupling by striking of the upper light with the screen corrected in the vessel of Malchut, which is called the first look. And as written above in Item 61, from the restriction onward the measure of the upper light that the degree receives depends upon and is measured by the measure of the magnitude of the reflected light that rises through the coupling by striking on the screen; for this reflected light is what connects and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:67
items.html:
The reflected light of the Rosh is not an actual vessel, but a root for the vessels.
And you must remember all that is explained here in Inner Light on this matter of the clothing of the reflected light upon the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head]; and the main point is that this is not regarded as an actual clothing in practice, since it rises from below upward, which means, as it were, an opposition to clothing in the coarseness of the vessels. Yet, even so, this reflected light is found to widen the vessel of Malchut of the Rosh into ten Sefirot of her own and within herself, and these became actual vessels of reception in practice. And we have already elaborated on this (in Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 30).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:68
items.html:
The third kind is the reflected light that inverts from the Peh downward and clothes the ten Sefirot of the Guf down to the Tabur
The third kind of the vessels is what was brought above (Item 65), that the reflected light of the Rosh [head], which is the aforementioned second kind — although it is itself not an aspect of clothing at all — nevertheless inverts and becomes an aspect of an actual vessel of reception in practice. And this third kind is always called by the name Guf [body] of the Partzuf, and the aforementioned second kind is always called by the name Rosh of the Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:69
items.html:
The fourth kind is the vessels from the Tabur downward
The fourth kind is vessels that are below the Tabur, which are regarded as ten Sefirot of reflected light in which there is no direct light. For the matter of the aforementioned third kind applies only up to the Tabur, which is the place of the first nine Sefirot of the Guf [body]; but from the Tabur downward, which is the place of the Malchut of the Guf, they are not considered vessels of reception.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:70
items.html:
The rejection and the clothing that the screen brought about in the Rosh in potential were revealed in the Guf in actuality — the clothing from the Peh to the Tabur and the rejection from the Tabur downward
And the reason is that the Rosh [head] and the Guf [body] are regarded as the relation of the “potential” to the “actual”, for everything that is included in the Rosh in potential is revealed in the Guf in actuality. Therefore these two actions that the screen brought about in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh — namely, the restraint upon the upper light so that it shall not expand to phase four, who is Malchut, and the clothing that it made by the force of the rising reflected light — both of them were in the Rosh only in the aspect of “potential”, as above. Indeed, the place of the revelation of these two actions is in the Guf: the aspect of the clothing that was in potential in the Rosh is found revealed in actuality above the Tabur of the Guf, and the aspect of the restraint upon Malchut is found revealed in actuality below the Tabur of the Guf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:71
items.html:
The fifth kind is the vessels of the first expansion, called coarse light
The fifth kind is vessels that were emptied of the upper light, which are called coarse light. For after the ten Sefirot of the Guf [body] expanded from the Peh [mouth] of AK down to the Tabur, as above in Item 68, in the aspect of the third kind, afterwards the upper light again departed from within them and the vessels remained empty of light. And there is here a great discernment: for in the aforementioned first expansion, although they are regarded there as actual vessels of reception in practice, as above (in Item 68), even so they are not yet considered actual vessels, because of the great importance that the vessels have there, as written in Inner Light here (Chapter 6, Item 5). And therefore the ARI says there that the vessels and the light within them are mixed. Indeed, after the light departed from within them their coarseness became discernible, and a difference came about between light and vessel; and therefore these vessels are called by the name coarse light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:72
items.html:
The sixth kind is vessels that were emptied of their lights, and the records that remained enliven them
The sixth kind is vessels that were emptied after the departure, and there remained in them records of the lights that departed, which records enliven and sustain the vessels so that they shall be fit to attain their lights as at first. And likewise they illuminate for the Partzuf that comes after them. As brought here in the words of the ARI (Chapter 2, Item 1; and see there in Item 8, and in Chapter 4, Item 2).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:73
items.html:
The seventh kind is vessels that were emptied and in which no records remained
The seventh kind is vessels that were emptied after the departure, and in which no records of the lights that departed remained. And these are the last phases of every Partzuf and expansion, for the last phase leaves no record. As brought in the words of the ARI (Chapter 2, Item 6). And this indeed is in the manner explained above (in Item 43).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:74
items.html:
The eighth kind is vessels that were made fit for the need of the second Partzuf that comes after it
The eighth kind is the aspect of the vessels that were prepared and made fit in a Partzuf for the need of the second Partzuf that comes after it, as brought in the words of the ARI (in Chapter 4, Item 6). And even the vessel of Keter [crown], of which the ARI says there that it was not made in the first Partzuf but only in the second Partzuf itself — even so, the aspect of the vessel of Keter from the aspect of the male was prepared from the first Partzuf, as written in Inner Light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:75
items.html:
The aforementioned kind of vessels are the male vessels in the second Partzuf
Now the aforementioned eighth kind are the male vessels for the need of the second Partzuf, and they come from the records that the lights left in the vessels after their departure; for from the coarse light included in those records the male vessels were made, as written in Inner Light (Chapter 2, Item 3), and as brought in the words of the ARI in the Gate of Mati Ve’lo Mati [reaching and not reaching], Chapter 3.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:76
items.html:
The ninth kind is vessels prepared in a Partzuf as female vessels for the second Partzuf
The ninth kind is the female vessels that were prepared in the first Partzuf for the need of the second Partzuf. And they were made from the aspect of the sparks that fall into the empty vessels after the light has departed from them, which come from the illumination of the coupling that is in the phase above the empty vessel, as written in the words of the ARI (Chapter 4, Item 3). And since in the second Partzuf the lights were exchanged there, so that the light of Hochma comes in the vessel of Keter [crown], and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, and the light of ZA in the vessel of Bina, etc., therefore they needed vessels there that would be equal to their aspect. For this reason these sparks were prepared, so that the sparks that fell from the level of Bina into the empty vessel of the level of Hochma became a vessel for the light of Bina that comes in the vessel of Hochma; and the sparks that fell from the level of ZA into the vessel of the level of Bina became a vessel for the light of ZA that comes in the vessel of Bina; and so forth in this way.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:77
items.html:
The tenth kind is external vessels for surrounding light
The tenth kind is the external vessels for surrounding light. For surrounding light is not received by a degree unless it receives it from the phase that is above the phase corresponding to it in the Rosh [head]. Therefore it likewise requires a vessel suited to this light, that is, that the vessel too shall be from the phase that is above the phase corresponding to it in the Rosh. And if the degree is from phase four, it requires a vessel that shall be from phase three; and if it is from phase three, it requires a vessel that shall be from phase two; and so forth in this way. And therefore the vessels of surrounding light are called external vessels, for with respect to vessels it is always regarded that whatever is more refined than its fellow is more external than its fellow. As written at length in Inner Light, Chapter 5, Item 3.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 4:78
items.html:
The aforementioned vessels come to the degree at the time of the refinement
Now these external vessels are attained by the degree only by way of ascent to the degree above it, which takes place at the time of the ascent of the lights to the Emanator. As brought in the words of the ARI here (Chapter 6, Item 15); and see there in Inner Light.
